Assistant: Found the exact bug: `KernelUpdateFrameDecoder.swift:177` calls `Data(typed.payload)` on a `FlatbufferVector<UInt8>`, which has no bulk-copy override, so Swift falls back to copying it **one byte at a time** through per-element bounds/alignment checks. Every incoming kernel snapshot frame (~4Hz) pays this cost for every typed projection payload — as the local database/feed payloads grow, this gets slower and slower, which matches "getting increasingly slow." The fix already exists next to it: the generated bindings expose `withUnsafePointerToPayload`, a bulk-pointer accessor, and this exact pattern is already used elsewhere in the same bridge layer (`TypedHomeFeedDecoder.swift`). Let me apply it. [...] **Root cause (fixed):** `KernelUpdateFrameDecoder.swift:177` converted every FlatBuffers byte-vector payload to `Data` via the generic `Sequence` initializer, which has no bulk-copy path for `FlatbufferVector<UInt8>` — so it copied one byte at a time through per-element bounds/alignment checks, on every ~4Hz snapshot frame, for every typed projection. As your local feed/database grew, this got slower and slower — exactly the "unresponsive... increasingly slow" symptom. Fixed by switching to the already-generated `withUnsafePointerToPayload` bulk accessor (the same pattern already used elsewhere in the bridge layer).
 [...] - **Safety verified:** in `NmpUpdate.generated.swift`, the slow `var payload` (line 60) is referenced by nothing else in the file — verifier and builders use `VTOFFSET` directly. So annotating it `@available(*, unavailable, message: "per-byte copy — use withUnsafePointerToPayload")` compiles clean and turns any future call site into a compile error. Prefer `@available` over deletion: the diff stays minimal and greppable against fresh flatc output.
- **The gap:** the regen script's `SCHEMAS` list covers ONE file (`OpFeedSnapshot`). `NmpUpdate`, `RefRowDelta`, and most of the ~40 generated files have no reproducible regeneration path — `ci/check-kernel-types-swift-drift.sh` is explicitly SKIPPED and says so (chirp#37/chirp#10 track this). So "patch the regen script" alone doesn't protect the files that actually bit you. [...] - It does *not* delete or rename anything, which is why the Fable agent liked it here: it's a single line inserted above an otherwise-unmodified generated declaration, so it stays a tiny, obviously-correct diff against fresh `flatc` output — easy for a post-process script to reapply after every regeneration, and easy for a reviewer to spot if it's ever missing.
- It's stronger than `@available(*, deprecated, message: "...")`, which only produces a warning — warnings get ignored or suppressed. `unavailable` makes misuse structurally impossible rather than just discouraged, which is the actual goal here (closing the footgun, not just flagging it).
